subject: Common phrases and features for statements
notes: kb/Work/PB401.md - rule 1, 'When the range of values is defined by numeric literals, the range of values includes literal-1, literal-2, and all algebraic values between literal-1 and literal-2'. A numeric range lowers to the inclusive ALGEBRAIC pair `subject >= lo && subject <= hi` over the numeric channel, names no collating sequence, and sets NO exception condition in either direction - which is what makes rule 1 observably different from rule 2 and is measured as such: PBR10 (inverted numeric identifier ends: empty, no EC), PBR11 (arithmetic-expression ends 1+1 THRU 8+2 containing 5 algebraically), PBR12/PBR13 (literal ends both directions), and the golden's NUMINV/ARITH arms. The rule-1/rule-2 split is written down ONCE, as CollatingSelection.IsCollatedThroughRange over the range's class, so a site cannot implement one rule and leave the other to a second author; before it, an arithmetic-expression-ended range was classified ALPHANUMERIC (its operand answered 'no category') and took rule 2's collating treatment.
